terminal.integrated.allowChords.markdownDescription: Whether or not to allow chord keybindings in the terminal. Note that when this is true and the keystroke results in a chord it will bypass `#terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell#`, setting this to false is particularly useful when you want ctrl+k to go to your shell (not VSLight).

terminal.integrated.allowMnemonics.markdownDescription: Whether to allow menubar mnemonics (for example Alt+F) to trigger the open of the menubar. Note that this will cause all alt keystrokes to skip the shell when true. This does nothing on macOS.

terminal.integrated.env.osx.markdownDescription: Object with environment variables that will be added to the VSLight process to be used by the terminal on macOS. Set to `null` to delete the environment variable.

terminal.integrated.env.linux.markdownDescription: Object with environment variables that will be added to the VSLight process to be used by the terminal on Linux. Set to `null` to delete the environment variable.

terminal.integrated.env.windows.markdownDescription: Object with environment variables that will be added to the VSLight process to be used by the terminal on Windows. Set to `null` to delete the environment variable.

terminal.integrated.environmentChangesRe.markdownDescription: Whether to relaunch terminals automatically if extensions want to contribute to their environment and have not been interacted with yet.

terminal.integrated.showExitAlert.description: Controls whether to show the alert "The terminal process terminated with exit code" when exit code is non-zero.

terminal.integrated.windowsUseConptyDll.markdownDescription: Whether to use the conpty.dll (v1.25.260303002) shipped with VSLight, instead of the one bundled with Windows.

terminal.integrated.splitCwd.description: Controls the working directory a split terminal starts with.
enumDescriptions: A new split terminal will use the workspace root as the working directory. In a multi-root workspace a choice for which root folder to use is offered.
A new split terminal will use the working directory that the parent terminal started with.
On macOS and Linux, a new split terminal will use the working directory of the parent terminal. On Windows, this behaves the same as initial.

terminal.integrated.wordSeparators.markdownDescription: A string containing all characters to be considered word separators when double-clicking to select word and in the fallback 'word' link detection. Since this is used for link detection, including characters such as `:` that are used when detecting links will cause the line and column part of links like `file:10:5` to be ignored.

terminal.integrated.enableFileLinks.description: Whether to enable file links in terminals. Links can be slow when working on a network drive in particular because each file link is verified against the file system. Changing this will take effect only in new terminals.
enumDescriptions: Always off.
Always on.
Enable only when not in a remote workspace.

terminal.integrated.allowedLinkSchemes.description: An array of strings containing the URI schemes that the terminal is allowed to open links for. By default, only a small subset of possible schemes are allowed for security reasons.

enumDescriptions: Version 6 of Unicode. This is an older version which should work better on older systems.
Version 11 of Unicode. This version provides better support on modern systems that use modern versions of Unicode.
terminal.integrated.unicodeVersion.description: Controls what version of Unicode to use when evaluating the width of characters in the terminal. If you experience emoji or other wide characters not taking up the right amount of space or backspace either deleting too much or too little then you may want to try tweaking this setting.

terminal.integrated.enablePersistentSess.description: Persist terminal sessions/history for the workspace across window reloads.

terminal.integrated.persistentSessionRev.markdownDescription:
When the terminal process must be shut down (for example on window or application close), this determines when the previous terminal session contents/history should be restored and processes be recreated when the workspace is next opened.

Caveats:

- Restoring of the process current working directory depends on whether it is supported by the shell.
- Time to persist the session during shutdown is limited, so it may be aborted when using high-latency remote connections.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Revive the processes after the last window is closed on Windows/Linux or when the `workbench.action.quit` command is triggered (command palette, keybinding, menu).
Revive the processes after the last window is closed on Windows/Linux or when the `workbench.action.quit` command is triggered (command palette, keybinding, menu), or when the window is closed.
Never restore the terminal buffers or recreate the process.

terminal.integrated.hideOnStartup.description: Whether to hide the terminal view on startup, avoiding creating a terminal when there are no persistent sessions.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Never hide the terminal view on startup.
Only hide the terminal when there are no persistent sessions restored.
Always hide the terminal, even when there are persistent sessions restored.

terminal.integrated.hideOnLastClosed.description: Whether to hide the terminal view when the last terminal is closed. This will only happen when the terminal is the only visible view in the view container.

terminal.integrated.customGlyphs.markdownDescription:
Whether to draw custom glyphs instead of using the font for the following unicode ranges:

- Box Drawing (U+2500-U+257F)
- Block Elements (U+2580-U+259F)
- Braille Patterns (U+2800-U+28FF)
- Powerline Symbols (U+E0A0-U+E0D4, Private Use Area)
- Progress Indicators (U+EE00-U+EE0B, Private Use Area)
- Git Branch Symbols (U+F5D0-U+F60D, Private Use Area)
- Symbols for Legacy Computing (U+1FB00-U+1FBFF)

This will typically result in better rendering with continuous lines, even when line height and letter spacing is used. This feature only works when `#terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration#` is enabled.

terminal.integrated.rescaleOverlappingGl.markdownDescription: Whether to rescale glyphs horizontally that are a single cell wide but have glyphs that would overlap following cell(s). This typically happens for ambiguous width characters (eg. the roman numeral characters U+2160+) which aren't featured in monospace fonts. Emoji glyphs are never rescaled.

terminal.integrated.enableKittyKeyboardP.markdownDescription: Whether to enable the kitty keyboard protocol, which allows a program in the terminal to request more detailed keyboard input reporting. This can, for example, enable `Shift+Enter` to be handled by the program.

terminal.integrated.enableWin32InputMode.markdownDescription: Whether to enable the win32 input mode, which provides enhanced keyboard input support on Windows.

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.ena.markdownDescription:
Determines whether or not shell integration is auto-injected to support features like enhanced command tracking and current working directory detection. 

Shell integration works by injecting the shell with a startup script. The script gives VSLight insight into what is happening within the terminal.

Supported shells:

- Linux/macOS: bash, fish, pwsh, zsh
 - Windows: pwsh, git bash

This setting applies only when terminals are created, so you will need to restart your terminals for it to take effect.

 Note that the script injection may not work if you have custom arguments defined in the terminal profile, have enabled `#editor.accessibilitySupport#`, have a [complex bash `PROMPT_COMMAND`](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/integrated-terminal#_complex-bash-promptcommand), or other unsupported setup. To disable decorations, see `#terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.decorationsEnabled#`

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.dec.markdownDescription: When shell integration is enabled, adds a decoration for each command.
enumDescriptions: Show decorations in the gutter (left) and overview ruler (right)
Show gutter decorations to the left of the terminal
Show overview ruler decorations to the right of the terminal
Do not show decorations

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.tim.markdownDescription: Configures the duration in milliseconds to wait for shell integration after launch before declaring it's not there. The default value `-1` uses a variable wait time based on whether shell integration injection is enabled and whether it's a remote window. Values between 1 and 499 are clamped to 500ms. Consider setting this to a large value if your shell starts very slowly.

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.qui.markdownDescription: When shell integration is enabled, enables quick fixes for terminal commands that appear as a lightbulb or sparkle icon to the left of the prompt.

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.env.markdownDescription: Controls whether to report the shell environment, enabling its use in features such as `#terminal.integrated.suggest.enabled#`. This may cause a slowdown when printing your shell's prompt.

terminal.integrated.smoothScrolling.markdownDescription: Controls whether the terminal will scroll using an animation.

terminal.integrated.ignoreBracketedPaste.markdownDescription: Controls whether the terminal will ignore bracketed paste mode even if the terminal was put into the mode, omitting the `\x1b[200~` and `\x1b[201~` sequences when pasting. This is useful when the shell is not respecting the mode which can happen in sub-shells for example.

terminal.integrated.enableImages.markdownDescription: Enables image support in the terminal, this will only work when `#terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration#` is enabled. Sixel and iTerm's inline image protocol are supported on Linux and macOS. The kitty graphics protocol is supported on all platforms. On Windows, all image protocols will only work for versions of ConPTY >= v2 which is shipped with Windows itself, see also `#terminal.integrated.windowsUseConptyDll#`. Images will currently not be restored between window reloads/reconnects. When enabled, transparency mode is also turned on in the terminal.

terminal.integrated.focusAfterRun.markdownDescription: Controls whether the terminal, accessible buffer, or neither will be focused after `Terminal: Run Selected Text In Active Terminal` has been run.

terminal.integrated.allowInUntrustedWork.markdownDescription:
Controls whether terminals can be created in an untrusted workspace.

**This feature bypasses a security protection that prevents terminals from launching in untrusted workspaces. The reason this is a security risk is because shells are often set up to potentially execute code automatically based on the contents of the current working directory. This should be safe to use provided your shell is set up in such a way that code execution in the folder never happens.**

terminal.integrated.developer.ptyHost.la.description: Simulated latency in milliseconds applied to all calls made to the pty host. This is useful for testing terminal behavior under high latency conditions.

terminal.integrated.developer.ptyHost.st.description: Simulated startup delay in milliseconds for the pty host process. This is useful for testing terminal initialization under slow startup conditions.

terminal.integrated.developer.devMode.description: Enable developer mode for the terminal. This shows additional debug information and visualizations for shell integration sequences.

terminal.integrated.accessibleViewPreser.markdownDescription: Controls whether the cursor position is preserved in the terminal's accessible view.
enumDescriptions: Always position the cursor at the bottom of the buffer.
Preserve the cursor position on reopen until new terminal content arrives.
Always preserve the cursor position, including when new terminal content arrives.

terminal.integrated.accessibleViewFocusO.markdownDescription: Focus the terminal accessible view when a command is executed.

terminal.integrated.autoReplies.markdownDescription:
A set of messages that, when encountered in the terminal, will be automatically responded to. Provided the message is specific enough, this can help automate away common responses.

Remarks:

- Use `"Terminate batch job (Y/N)": "Y\r"` to automatically respond to the terminate batch job prompt on Windows.
- The message includes escape sequences so the reply might not happen with styled text.
- Each reply can only happen once every second.
- Use `"\r"` in the reply to mean the enter key.
- To unset a default key, set the value to null.
- Restart VSLight if new don't apply.

oneOf.description: The reply to send to the process.

terminal.integrated.initialHint.markdownDescription: Controls if the first terminal without input will show a hint about available actions when it is focused. This will only show when `#terminal.integrated.sendKeybindingsToShell#` is disabled.

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.sho.markdownDescription: Whether to show the command guide when hovering over a command in the terminal.

terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.his.markdownDescription: Controls the number of recently used commands to keep in the terminal command history. Set to 0 to disable terminal command history.

terminal.integrated.enableNotifications.description: Controls whether notifications sent from the terminal via OSC 99 are shown. This uses notifications inside the product instead of desktop notifications. Sounds, icons and filtering are not supported.

terminal.integrated.resizeDimensionsOver.markdownDescription: Whether to show a visual overlay with the terminal's columns and rows when it is resized.

terminal.integrated.stickyScroll.enabled.markdownDescription: Shows the current command at the top of the terminal. This feature requires [shell integration](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/shell-integration) to be activated. See `#terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled#`.

terminal.integrated.stickyScroll.maxLine.markdownDescription: Defines the maximum number of sticky lines to show. Sticky scroll lines will never exceed 40% of the viewport regardless of this setting.

terminal.integrated.stickyScroll.ignored.markdownDescription: A list of commands that should not trigger sticky scroll. When a command from this list is detected, the sticky scroll overlay will be hidden.

terminal.integrated.suggest.enabled.markdownDescription: Enables terminal IntelliSense suggestions (also known as autocomplete) for supported shells (Windows PowerShell, PowerShell v7+, zsh, bash, fish). This requires `#terminal.integrated.shellIntegration.enabled#` to be enabled and working or [manually installed](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/shell-integration#_manual-installation-install).

terminal.integrated.suggest.quickSuggest.markdownDescription: Controls whether suggestions should automatically show up while typing. Also be aware of the `#terminal.integrated.suggest.suggestOnTriggerCharacters#`-setting which controls if suggestions are triggered by special characters.

commands.description: Enable quick suggestions for commands, the first word in a command line input.

arguments.description: Enable quick suggestions for arguments, anything after the first word in a command line input.

unknown.description: Enable quick suggestions when it's unclear what the best suggestion is, if this is on files and folders will be suggested as a fallback.

terminal.integrated.suggest.suggestOnTri.markdownDescription: Controls whether suggestions should automatically show up when typing trigger characters.

terminal.integrated.suggest.runOnEnter.markdownDescription: Controls whether suggestions should run immediately when `Enter` (not `Tab`) is used to accept the result.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Run on `Enter` when the suggestion is typed in its entirety.
Run on `Enter` when the suggestion is typed in its entirety or when a file is typed without its extension included.

terminal.integrated.suggest.selectionMod.markdownDescription: Controls how suggestion selection works in the integrated terminal.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Partially select a suggestion when automatically triggering IntelliSense. `Tab` can be used to accept the first suggestion, only after navigating the suggestions via `Down` will `Enter` also accept the active suggestion.
Always select a suggestion when automatically triggering IntelliSense. `Enter` or `Tab` can be used to accept the first suggestion.
Never select a suggestion when automatically triggering IntelliSense. The list must be navigated via `Down` before `Enter` or `Tab` can be used to accept the active suggestion.

terminal.integrated.suggest.windowsExecu.markdownDescription:
A set of windows command executable extensions that will be included as suggestions in the terminal.

Many executables are included by default, listed below:

- bat
- cmd

window.restoreWindows.description: Controls how windows and editors within are being restored when opening.

window.restoreFullscreen.description: Controls whether a window should restore to full screen mode if it was exited in full screen mode.

window.zoomLevel.markdownDescription: Adjust the default zoom level for all windows. Each increment above `0` (e.g. `1`) or below (e.g. `-1`) represents zooming `20%` larger or smaller. You can also enter decimals to adjust the zoom level with a finer granularity. See `#window.zoomPerWindow#` for configuring if the 'Zoom In' and 'Zoom Out' commands apply the zoom level to all windows or only the active window.

window.zoomPerWindow.markdownDescription: Controls if the 'Zoom In' and 'Zoom Out' commands apply the zoom level to all windows or only the active window. See `#window.zoomLevel#` for configuring a default zoom level for all windows.

enumDescriptions: Open new windows in the center of the screen.
Open new windows with same dimension as last active one.
Open new windows with same dimension as last active one with an offset position.
Open new windows maximized.
Open new windows in full screen mode.
window.newWindowDimensions.description: Controls the dimensions of opening a new window when at least one window is already opened. Note that this setting does not have an impact on the first window that is opened. The first window will always restore the size and location as you left it before closing.

window.closeWhenEmpty.description: Controls whether closing the last editor should also close the window. This setting only applies for windows that do not show folders.

window.doubleClickIconToClose.markdownDescription: If enabled, this setting will close the window when the application icon in the title bar is double-clicked. The window will not be able to be dragged by the icon. This setting is effective only if `#window.titleBarStyle#` is set to `custom`.

window.titleBarStyle.description: Adjust the appearance of the window title bar to be native by the OS or custom. Changes require a full restart to apply.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Automatically changes custom title bar visibility.
Hide custom titlebar in full screen. When not in full screen, automatically change custom title bar visibility.
Hide custom titlebar when `#window.titleBarStyle#` is set to `native`.
window.customTitleBarVisibility.markdownDescription: Adjust when the custom title bar should be shown. The custom title bar can be hidden when in full screen mode with `windowed`. The custom title bar can only be hidden in non full screen mode with `never` when `#window.titleBarStyle#` is set to `native`.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Matches the context menu style to the title bar style defined in `#window.titleBarStyle#`.
window.menuStyle.markdownDescription: Adjust the context menu appearances to either be native by the OS, custom, or inherited from the title bar style defined in `#window.titleBarStyle#`.

window.dialogStyle.description: Adjust the appearance of dialogs to be native by the OS or custom.

window.nativeTabs.description: Enables macOS native window tabs. Note that changes require a full restart to apply and that native tabs will disable a custom title bar style if configured.

window.nativeFullScreen.description: Controls if native full-screen should be used on macOS. Disable this option to prevent macOS from creating a new space when going full-screen.

window.clickThroughInactive.description: If enabled, clicking on an inactive window will both activate the window and trigger the element under the mouse if it is clickable. If disabled, clicking anywhere on an inactive window will activate it only and a second click is required on the element.

telemetry.enableCrashReporter.description:
Enable crash reports to be collected. This helps us improve stability. 
This option requires restart to take effect.
telemetry.enableCrashReporter.markdownDeprecationMessage: If this setting is false, no telemetry will be sent regardless of the new setting's value. Deprecated due to being combined into the `#telemetry.telemetryLevel#` setting.
telemetry.enableCrashReporter.deprecationMessage: If this setting is false, no telemetry will be sent regardless of the new setting's value. Deprecated due to being combined into the telemetry.telemetryLevel setting.

keyboard.touchbar.enabled.description: Enables the macOS touchbar buttons on the keyboard if available.

keyboard.touchbar.ignored.markdownDescription: A set of identifiers for entries in the touchbar that should not show up (for example `workbench.action.navigateBack`).

security.promptForLocalFileProtocolHandl.markdownDescription: If enabled, a dialog will ask for confirmation whenever a local file or workspace is about to open through a protocol handler.

security.promptForRemoteFileProtocolHand.markdownDescription: If enabled, a dialog will ask for confirmation whenever a remote file or workspace is about to open through a protocol handler.

keyboard.dispatch.markdownDescription: Controls the dispatching logic for key presses to use either `code` (recommended) or `keyCode`.

enumDescriptions: Sends usage data, errors, and crash reports.
Sends general error telemetry and crash reports.
Sends OS level crash reports.
Disables all product telemetry.
telemetry.telemetryLevel.markdownDescription:
Controls VSLight telemetry, first-party extension telemetry, and participating third-party extension telemetry. Some third party extensions might not respect this setting. Consult the specific extension's documentation to be sure. Telemetry helps us better understand how VSLight is performing, where improvements need to be made, and how features are being used. Read more about the [data we collect](https://aka.ms/vscode-telemetry). A full restart of the application is necessary for crash reporting changes to take effect.

 

The following table outlines the data sent with each setting:

|       | Crash Reports | Error Telemetry | Usage Data |
|:------|:-------------:|:---------------:|:----------:|
| all   |       ✓       |        ✓        |     ✓      |
| error |       ✓       |        ✓        |     -      |
| crash |       ✓       |        -        |     -      |
| off   |       -       |        -        |     -      |


 

****Note:*** If this setting is 'off', no telemetry will be sent regardless of other telemetry settings. If this setting is set to anything except 'off' and telemetry is disabled with deprecated settings, no telemetry will be sent.*

description.value: Controls the level of telemetry.

enumDescriptions.value: Sends usage data, errors, and crash reports.
Sends general error telemetry and crash reports.
Sends OS level crash reports.
Disables all product telemetry.

telemetry.feedback.enabled.description: Enable feedback mechanisms such as the issue reporter, surveys, and other feedback options.

description.value: Enable feedback mechanisms such as the issue reporter, surveys, and other feedback options.

telemetry.enableTelemetry.markdownDescription: Enable diagnostic data to be collected. This helps us to better understand how VSLight is performing and where improvements need to be made.
telemetry.enableTelemetry.markdownDeprecationMessage: If this setting is false, no telemetry will be sent regardless of the new setting's value. Deprecated in favor of the `#telemetry.telemetryLevel#` setting.
telemetry.enableTelemetry.deprecationMessage: If this setting is false, no telemetry will be sent regardless of the new setting's value. Deprecated in favor of the telemetry.telemetryLevel setting.

enumDescriptions: Native widget colors match the system colors.
Use light native widget colors for light color themes and dark for dark color themes.
Use light native widget colors.
Use dark native widget colors.
window.systemColorTheme.markdownDescription:
Set the color mode for native UI elements such as native dialogs, menus and title bar. Even if your OS is configured in light color mode, you can select a dark system color theme for the window. You can also configure to automatically adjust based on the `#workbench.colorTheme#` setting.

Note: This setting is ignored when `#window.autoDetectColorScheme#` is enabled.

application.experimental.rendererProfili.markdownDescription: When enabled, slow renderers are automatically profiled.

onboarding.developerMode.description: Map of onboarding scenario/tour id to whether developer mode is enabled for it. When enabled for a scenario, that onboarding tour ignores usage-based eligibility checks (such as how many sessions you have started), previously persisted shown state, and any linked experiment (so it is shown even if the experiment is not running or you are in the control group). It does not override the `#onboarding.enabled#` setting. The tour is still shown at most once per window session, so reload the window to show it again.

onboarding.developerModeVariations.description: Map of onboarding scenario/tour id to the variation used while developer mode is enabled for that scenario. An empty value uses the experiment-selected or default variation.

css.customData.markdownDescription:
A list of relative file paths pointing to JSON files following the [custom data format](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-css-languageservice/blob/master/docs/customData.md).

VSLight loads custom data on startup to enhance its CSS support for CSS custom properties (variables), at-rules, pseudo-classes, and pseudo-elements you specify in the JSON files.

The file paths are relative to workspace and only workspace folder settings are considered.

emmet.showExpandedAbbreviation.markdownDescription:
Shows expanded Emmet abbreviations as suggestions.
The option `"inMarkupAndStylesheetFilesOnly"` applies to html, haml, jade, slim, xml, xsl, css, scss, sass, less and stylus.
The option `"always"` applies to all parts of the file regardless of markup/css.

emmet.showAbbreviationSuggestions.markdownDescription: Shows possible Emmet abbreviations as suggestions. Not applicable in stylesheets or when emmet.showExpandedAbbreviation is set to `"never"`.

emmet.includeLanguages.markdownDescription:
Enable Emmet abbreviations in languages that are not supported by default. Add a mapping here between the language and Emmet supported language.
 For example: `{"vue-html": "html", "javascript": "javascriptreact"}`

emmet.variables.markdownDescription: Variables to be used in Emmet snippets.

emmet.syntaxProfiles.markdownDescription: Define profile for specified syntax or use your own profile with specific rules.

emmet.excludeLanguages.markdownDescription: An array of languages where Emmet abbreviations should not be expanded.

items.markdownDescription: A path containing Emmet syntaxProfiles and/or snippets.

emmet.extensionsPath.markdownDescription:
An array of paths, where each path can contain Emmet syntaxProfiles and/or snippet files.
In case of conflicts, the profiles/snippets of later paths will override those of earlier paths.
See https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/emmet for more information and an example snippet file.

emmet.triggerExpansionOnTab.markdownDescription: When enabled, Emmet abbreviations are expanded when pressing TAB, even when completions do not show up. When disabled, completions that show up can still be accepted by pressing TAB.

emmet.useInlineCompletions.markdownDescription: If `true`, Emmet will use inline completions to suggest expansions. To prevent the non-inline completion item provider from showing up as often while this setting is `true`, turn `#editor.quickSuggestions#` to `inline` or `off` for the `other` item.

emmet.preferences.markdownDescription: Preferences used to modify behavior of some actions and resolvers of Emmet.

css.propertyEnd.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the end of CSS property when expanding CSS abbreviations.

sass.propertyEnd.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the end of CSS property when expanding CSS abbreviations in Sass files.

stylus.propertyEnd.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the end of CSS property when expanding CSS abbreviations in Stylus files.

css.valueSeparator.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the between CSS property and value when expanding CSS abbreviations.

sass.valueSeparator.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the between CSS property and value when expanding CSS abbreviations in Sass files.

stylus.valueSeparator.markdownDescription: Symbol to be placed at the between CSS property and value when expanding CSS abbreviations in Stylus files.

bem.elementSeparator.markdownDescription: Element separator used for classes when using the BEM filter.

bem.modifierSeparator.markdownDescription: Modifier separator used for classes when using the BEM filter.

filter.commentBefore.markdownDescription: A definition of comment that should be placed before matched element when comment filter is applied.

filter.commentAfter.markdownDescription: A definition of comment that should be placed after matched element when comment filter is applied.

filter.commentTrigger.markdownDescription: A comma-separated list of attribute names that should exist in the abbreviation for the comment filter to be applied.

format.noIndentTags.markdownDescription: An array of tag names that should never get inner indentation.

format.forceIndentationForTags.markdownDescription: An array of tag names that should always get inner indentation.

profile.allowCompactBoolean.markdownDescription: If `true`, compact notation of boolean attributes are produced.

css.webkitProperties.markdownDescription: Comma separated CSS properties that get the `webkit` vendor prefix when used in Emmet abbreviation that starts with `-`. Set to empty string to always avoid the `webkit` prefix.

css.mozProperties.markdownDescription: Comma separated CSS properties that get the `moz` vendor prefix when used in Emmet abbreviation that starts with `-`. Set to empty string to always avoid the `moz` prefix.

css.oProperties.markdownDescription: Comma separated CSS properties that get the `o` vendor prefix when used in Emmet abbreviation that starts with `-`. Set to empty string to always avoid the `o` prefix.

css.msProperties.markdownDescription: Comma separated CSS properties that get the `ms` vendor prefix when used in Emmet abbreviation that starts with `-`. Set to empty string to always avoid the `ms` prefix.

css.fuzzySearchMinScore.markdownDescription: The minimum score (from 0 to 1) that fuzzy-matched abbreviation should achieve. Lower values may produce many false-positive matches, higher values may reduce possible matches.

output.inlineBreak.markdownDescription: The number of sibling inline elements needed for line breaks to be placed between those elements. If `0`, inline elements are always expanded onto a single line.

output.reverseAttributes.markdownDescription: If `true`, reverses attribute merging directions when resolving snippets.

output.selfClosingStyle.markdownDescription:
Style of self-closing tags: html (`
`), xml (`
`) or xhtml (`
`).

css.color.short.markdownDescription: If `true`, color values like `#f` will be expanded to `#fff` instead of `#ffffff`.

emmet.showSuggestionsAsSnippets.markdownDescription: If `true`, then Emmet suggestions will show up as snippets allowing you to order them as per `#editor.snippetSuggestions#` setting.

emmet.optimizeStylesheetParsing.markdownDescription: When set to `false`, the whole file is parsed to determine if current position is valid for expanding Emmet abbreviations. When set to `true`, only the content around the current position in CSS/SCSS/Less files is parsed.

git.path.markdownDescription: Path and filename of the git executable, e.g. `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe` (Windows). This can also be an array of string values containing multiple paths to look up.

enumDescriptions: Scan for both subfolders of the current opened folder and parent folders of open files.
Disable automatic repository scanning.
Scan for subfolders of the currently opened folder.
Scan for parent folders of open files.
git.autoRepositoryDetection.description: Configures when repositories should be automatically detected.

git.autofetch.markdownDescription: When set to true, commits will automatically be fetched from the default remote of the current Git repository. Setting to `all` will fetch from all remotes.

git.autofetchPeriod.markdownDescription: Duration in seconds between each automatic git fetch, when `#git.autofetch#` is enabled.

git.defaultBranchName.markdownDescription: The name of the default branch (example: main, trunk, development) when initializing a new Git repository. When set to empty, the default branch name configured in Git will be used. **Note:** Requires Git version `2.28.0` or later.

git.branchPrefix.description: Prefix used when creating a new branch.

git.branchProtection.markdownDescription: List of protected branches. By default, a prompt is shown before changes are committed to a protected branch. The prompt can be controlled using the `#git.branchProtectionPrompt#`  setting.

git.branchProtectionPrompt.description: Controls whether a prompt is being shown before changes are committed to a protected branch.
enumDescriptions: Always commit changes to the protected branch.
Always commit changes to a new branch.
Always prompt before changes are committed to a protected branch.

git.branchValidationRegex.description: A regular expression to validate new branch names.

git.branchWhitespaceChar.description: The character to replace whitespace in new branch names, and to separate segments of a randomly generated branch name.

git.branchRandomName.enable.description: Controls whether a random name is generated when creating a new branch.

git.branchRandomName.dictionary.markdownDescription: List of dictionaries used for the randomly generated branch name. Each value represents the dictionary used to generate the segment of the branch name. Supported dictionaries: `adjectives`, `animals`, `colors` and `numbers`.

enumDescriptions: A random adjective
A random animal name
A random color name
A random number between 100 and 999

git.confirmCommittedDelete.description: Confirm before deleting committed files with Git.

enumDescriptions: Count all changes.
Count only tracked changes.
Turn off counter.
Local branches
Tags
Remote branches

git.checkoutType.markdownDescription: Controls what type of Git refs are listed when running `Checkout to...`.

git.ignoreMissingGitWarning.description: Ignores the warning when Git is missing.

git.ignoreWindowsGit27Warning.description: Ignores the warning when Git 2.25 - 2.26 is installed on Windows.

git.ignoreLimitWarning.description: Ignores the warning when there are too many changes in a repository.

git.ignoreRebaseWarning.description: Ignores the warning when it looks like the branch might have been rebased when pulling.

git.defaultCloneDirectory.description: The default location to clone a Git repository.

git.useEditorAsCommitInput.description: Controls whether a full text editor will be used to author commit messages, whenever no message is provided in the commit input box.

git.verboseCommit.markdownDescription: Enable verbose output when `#git.useEditorAsCommitInput#` is enabled.

git.enableSmartCommit.description: Commit all changes when there are no staged changes.

Automatically stage tracked changes only.
git.smartCommitChanges.description: Control which changes are automatically staged by Smart Commit.

git.suggestSmartCommit.description: Suggests to enable smart commit (commit all changes when there are no staged changes).

git.enableCommitSigning.description: Enables commit signing with GPG, X.509, or SSH.

git.confirmEmptyCommits.description: Always confirm the creation of empty commits for the 'Git: Commit Empty' command.

git.decorations.enabled.description: Controls whether Git contributes colors and badges to the Explorer and the Open Editors view.

git.enableStatusBarSync.description: Controls whether the Git Sync command appears in the status bar.

git.followTagsWhenSync.description: Push all annotated tags when running the sync command.

git.replaceTagsWhenPull.description: Automatically replace the local tags with the remote tags in case of a conflict when running the pull command.

enumDescriptions: Check for any unsaved files.
Check only for unsaved staged files.
Disable this check.
git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeStash.description: Controls whether Git should check for unsaved files before stashing changes.

enumDescriptions: Check for any unsaved files.
Check only for unsaved staged files.
Disable this check.
git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeCommit.description: Controls whether Git should check for unsaved files before committing.

git.showInlineOpenFileAction.description: Controls whether to show an inline Open File action in the Git changes view.

git.showPushSuccessNotification.description: Controls whether to show a notification when a push is successful.

git.inputValidation.description: Controls whether to show commit message input validation diagnostics.

git.inputValidationLength.description: Controls the commit message length threshold for showing a warning.

git.inputValidationSubjectLength.markdownDescription: Controls the commit message subject length threshold for showing a warning. Unset it to inherit the value of `#git.inputValidationLength#`.

git.detectSubmodules.description: Controls whether to automatically detect Git submodules.

git.detectSubmodulesLimit.description: Controls the limit of Git submodules detected.

git.detectWorktrees.description: Controls whether to automatically detect Git worktrees.

git.detectWorktreesLimit.description: Controls the limit of Git worktrees detected.

git.worktreeIncludeFiles.markdownDescription: Configure [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) for files and folders that are included when creating a new worktree. Only files and folders that match the patterns and are listed in `.gitignore` will be copied to the newly created worktree.

git.alwaysShowStagedChangesResourceGroup.description: Always show the Staged Changes resource group.

git.alwaysSignOff.description: Controls the signoff flag for all commits.

git.ignoreSubmodules.description: Ignore modifications to submodules in the file tree.

git.ignoredRepositories.description: List of Git repositories to ignore.

git.scanRepositories.description: List of paths to search for Git repositories in.

git.showProgress.description: Controls whether Git actions should show progress.

git.rebaseWhenSync.description: Force Git to use rebase when running the sync command.

git.pullBeforeCheckout.description: Controls whether a branch that does not have outgoing commits is fast-forwarded before it is checked out.

git.fetchOnPull.description: When enabled, fetch all branches when pulling. Otherwise, fetch just the current one.

git.autoStash.description: Stash any changes before pulling and restore them after successful pull.

git.allowForcePush.description: Controls whether force push (with or without lease) is enabled.

git.useForcePushWithLease.description: Controls whether force pushing uses the safer force-with-lease variant.

git.useForcePushIfIncludes.markdownDescription: Controls whether force pushing uses the safer force-if-includes variant. Note: This setting requires the `#git.useForcePushWithLease#` setting to be enabled, and Git version `2.30.0` or later.

git.confirmForcePush.description: Controls whether to ask for confirmation before force-pushing.

git.allowNoVerifyCommit.description: Controls whether commits without running pre-commit and commit-msg hooks are allowed.

git.confirmNoVerifyCommit.description: Controls whether to ask for confirmation before committing without verification.

git.closeDiffOnOperation.description: Controls whether the diff editor should be automatically closed when changes are stashed, committed, discarded, staged, or unstaged.

git.openDiffOnClick.description: Controls whether the diff editor should be opened when clicking a change. Otherwise the regular editor will be opened.

git.supportCancellation.description: Controls whether a notification comes up when running the Sync action, which allows the user to cancel the operation.

git.branchSortOrder.description: Controls the sort order for branches.

enumDescriptions: All changes, tracked and untracked, appear together and behave equally.
Untracked changes appear separately in the Source Control view. They are also excluded from several actions.
Untracked changes are hidden and excluded from several actions.

git.requireGitUserConfig.description: Controls whether to require explicit Git user configuration or allow Git to guess if missing.

markdown.copyFiles.destination.markdownDescription:
Configures the path and file name of files created by copy/paste or drag and drop. This is a map of globs that match against a Markdown document path to the destination path where the new file should be created.

The destination path may use the following variables:

- `${documentDirName}` — Absolute parent directory path of the Markdown document, e.g. `/Users/me/myProject/docs`.
- `${documentRelativeDirName}` — Relative parent directory path of the Markdown document, e.g. `docs`. This is the same as `${documentDirName}` if the file is not part of a workspace.
- `${documentFileName}` — The full filename of the Markdown document, e.g. `README.md`.
- `${documentBaseName}` — The basename of the Markdown document, e.g. `README`.
- `${documentExtName}` — The extension of the Markdown document, e.g. `md`.
- `${documentFilePath}` — Absolute path of the Markdown document, e.g. `/Users/me/myProject/docs/README.md`.
- `${documentRelativeFilePath}` — Relative path of the Markdown document, e.g. `docs/README.md`. This is the same as `${documentFilePath}` if the file is not part of a workspace.
- `${documentWorkspaceFolder}` — The workspace folder for the Markdown document, e.g. `/Users/me/myProject`. This is the same as `${documentDirName}` if the file is not part of a workspace.
- `${fileName}` — The file name of the dropped file, e.g. `image.png`.
- `${fileExtName}` — The extension of the dropped file, e.g. `png`.
- `${unixTime}` — The current Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
- `${isoTime}` — The current time in ISO 8601 format, e.g. '2025-06-06T08:40:32.123Z'.

Specifies the folder path to the tsserver and `lib*.d.ts` files under a TypeScript install to use for IntelliSense, for example: `./node_modules/typescript/lib`.

- When specified as a user setting, the TypeScript version from `js/ts.tsdk.path` automatically replaces the built-in TypeScript version.
- When specified as a workspace setting, `js/ts.tsdk.path` allows you to switch to use that workspace version of TypeScript for IntelliSense with the `TypeScript: Select TypeScript version` command.

Type only named imports are sorted to the beginning of the import list. E.g. `import { type A, type Y, B, Z } from 'module';`

numericCollation.markdownDescription: Requires `organizeImports.unicodeCollation: 'unicode'`. Sort numeric strings by integer value.

accentCollation.markdownDescription: Requires `organizeImports.unicodeCollation: 'unicode'`. Compare characters with diacritical marks as unequal to base character.

caseFirst.markdownDescription: Requires `organizeImports.unicodeCollation: 'unicode'`, and `organizeImports.caseSensitivity` is not `caseInsensitive`. Indicates whether upper-case will sort before lower-case.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Upper-case comes before lower-case. E.g. ` A, a, B, b`.

allContributions.title: Get Started with Accessibility Features
allContributions.description: Learn the tools and shortcuts that make VSLight accessible. Note that some actions are not actionable from within the context of the walkthrough.

steps.title: Use the accessibility help dialog to learn about features
steps.description:
The accessibility help dialog provides information about what to expect from a feature and the commands/keybindings to operate them.
 With focus in an editor, terminal, or comment, the relevant dialog can be opened with the Open Accessibility Help command.
[Open Accessibility Help](command:editor.action.accessibilityHelp)

steps.title: Screen reader users can inspect content line by line, character by character in the accessible view.
steps.description:
The accessible view is available for the terminal, hovers, notifications, comments, and inline completions.
 With focus in any of those features, it can be opened with the Open Accessible View command.
[Open Accessible View](command:editor.action.accessibleView)

steps.title: Control the verbosity of aria labels
steps.description:
Screen reader verbosity settings exist for features around the workbench so that once a user is familiar with a feature, they can avoid hearing hints about how to operate it. For example, features for which an accessibility help dialog exists will indicate how to open the dialog until the verbosity setting for that feature has been disabled.
 These and other accessibility settings can be configured by running the Open Accessibility Settings command.
[Open Accessibility Settings](command:workbench.action.openAccessibilitySettings)

steps.title: Unlock productivity with the Command Palette
steps.description:
Run commands without reaching for your mouse to accomplish any task in VSLight.
[Open Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands)

steps.title: Customize your keyboard shortcuts
steps.description:
Once you have discovered your favorite commands, create custom keyboard shortcuts for instant access.
[Keyboard Shortcuts](command:toSide:workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings)

steps.title: Fine tune which accessibility signals you want to receive via audio or a braille device
steps.description:
Accessibility sounds and announcements are played around the workbench for different events.
 These can be discovered and configured using the List Signal Sounds and List Signal Announcements commands.
[List Signal Sounds](command:signals.sounds.help)
[List Signal Announcements](command:accessibility.announcement.help)

steps.title: Access the hover in the editor to get more information on a variable or symbol
steps.description:
While focus is in the editor on a variable or symbol, a hover can be focused with the Show or Open Hover command.
[Show or Focus Hover](command:editor.action.showHover)

steps.title: Navigate to symbols in a file
steps.description:
The Go to Symbol command is useful for navigating between important landmarks in a document.
[Go to Symbol](command:workbench.action.gotoSymbol)

steps.title: Use code folding to collapse blocks of code and focus on the code you're interested in.
steps.description:
Fold or unfold a code section with the Toggle Fold command.
[Toggle Fold](command:editor.toggleFold)
 Fold or unfold recursively with the Toggle Fold Recursively Command
[Toggle Fold Recursively](command:editor.toggleFoldRecursively)

steps.title: Use Intellisense to improve coding efficiency
steps.description:
Intellisense suggestions can be opened with the Trigger Intellisense command.
[Trigger Intellisense](command:editor.action.triggerSuggest)
 Inline intellisense suggestions can be triggered with Trigger Inline Suggestion
[Trigger Inline Suggestion](command:editor.action.inlineSuggest.trigger)
 Useful settings include editor.inlineCompletionsAccessibilityVerbose and editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion.

steps.title: Configure accessibility settings
steps.description:

[Open Accessibility Settings](command:workbench.action.openAccessibilitySettings)

steps.description:
Customize every aspect of VSLight.
[Open Settings](command:toSide:workbench.action.openSettings)

media.altText: VSLight Settings

steps.title: Code with extensions
steps.description:
Extensions are VSLight's power-ups. They range from handy productivity hacks, expanding out-of-the-box features, to adding completely new capabilities.
[Browse Popular Extensions](command:workbench.extensions.action.showPopularExtensions)

media.altText: VSLight extension marketplace with featured language extensions

steps.title: Learn the editor
steps.description:
Try selection, code navigation, suggestions and other editing features in an interactive playground.
[Open Editor Playground](command:workbench.action.showInteractivePlayground)

media.altText: Editor commands in the Command Palette.

steps.title: Built-in terminal
steps.description:
Quickly run shell commands and monitor build output, right next to your code.
[Open Terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal)

media.altText: Integrated terminal running a few npm commands

steps.title: Track your code with Git
steps.description:
Set up the built-in version control for your project to track your changes and collaborate with others.
[Clone Repository](command:git.clone)

media.altText: Source Control view.

steps.title: Track your code with Git
steps.description:
Set up the built-in version control for your project to track your changes and collaborate with others.
[Initialize Git Repository](command:git.init)

media.altText: Source Control view.

steps.title: Track your code with Git
steps.description:
No more looking up Git commands! Git and GitHub workflows are seamlessly integrated.
[Open Source Control](command:workbench.view.scm)

media.altText: Source Control view.

steps.title: Install Git
steps.description:
Install Git to track changes in your projects.
[Install Git](https://aka.ms/vscode-install-git)
[Reload window](command:workbench.action.reloadWindow) after installation to complete Git setup.

media.altText: Install Git.

steps.title: Automate your project tasks
steps.description:
Create tasks for your common workflows and enjoy the integrated experience of running scripts and automatically checking results.
[Run Auto-detected Tasks](command:workbench.action.tasks.runTask)

media.altText: Task runner.

steps.title: Customize your shortcuts
steps.description:
Once you have discovered your favorite commands, create custom keyboard shortcuts for instant access.
[Keyboard Shortcuts](command:toSide:workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings)

media.altText: Interactive shortcuts.

steps.title: Safely browse and edit code
steps.description:
[Workspace Trust](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/workspace-trust) lets you decide whether your project folders should **allow or restrict** automatic code execution __(required for extensions and tasks)__.
Opening a file/folder will prompt to grant trust. You can always [enable trust](command:toSide:workbench.trust.manage) later.

media.altText: Workspace Trust editor in Restricted mode and a primary button for switching to Trusted mode.

allSteps.title: Just the right amount of UI

nodes: The full menu bar is available in the dropdown menu to make room for your code. Toggle its appearance for faster access.

media.altText: Comparing menu dropdown with the visible menu bar.

nodes: Extensions are VSLight's power-ups. A growing number are becoming available in the web.

media.altText: VSLight extension marketplace with featured language extensions

allSteps.title: Rich support for all your languages

nodes: Code with syntax highlighting, inline suggestions and linting. While many languages are built-in, many more can be added as extensions.

media.altText: Language extensions

allSteps.title: Unlock productivity with the Command Palette

nodes: Run commands without reaching for your mouse to accomplish any task in VSLight.

media.altText: Command Palette overlay for searching and executing commands.

nodes: You're all set to start coding. You can open a local project or a remote repository to get your files into VSLight.

media.altText: Explorer view showing buttons for opening folder and cloning repository.

nodes: Navigate between files in an instant with one keystroke. Tip: Open multiple files by pressing the right arrow key.

media.altText: Go to file in quick search.

allSteps.title: Use the accessibility help dialog to learn about features

nodes: The accessibility help dialog provides information about what to expect from a feature and the commands/keybindings to operate them.
With focus in an editor, terminal, or comment, the relevant dialog can be opened with the Open Accessibility Help command.

allSteps.title: Screen reader users can inspect content line by line, character by character in the accessible view.

nodes: The accessible view is available for the terminal, hovers, notifications, comments, and inline completions.
With focus in any of those features, it can be opened with the Open Accessible View command.

allSteps.title: Control the verbosity of aria labels

nodes: Screen reader verbosity settings exist for features around the workbench so that once a user is familiar with a feature, they can avoid hearing hints about how to operate it. For example, features for which an accessibility help dialog exists will indicate how to open the dialog until the verbosity setting for that feature has been disabled.
These and other accessibility settings can be configured by running the Open Accessibility Settings command.

allSteps.title: Unlock productivity with the Command Palette

nodes: Run commands without reaching for your mouse to accomplish any task in VSLight.
Once you have discovered your favorite commands, create custom keyboard shortcuts for instant access.

allSteps.title: Fine tune which accessibility signals you want to receive via audio or a braille device

nodes: Accessibility sounds and announcements are played around the workbench for different events.
These can be discovered and configured using the List Signal Sounds and List Signal Announcements commands.

allSteps.title: Access the hover in the editor to get more information on a variable or symbol

nodes: While focus is in the editor on a variable or symbol, a hover can be focused with the Show or Open Hover command.

allSteps.title: Navigate to symbols in a file

nodes: The Go to Symbol command is useful for navigating between important landmarks in a document.

allSteps.title: Use code folding to collapse blocks of code and focus on the code you're interested in.

nodes: Fold or unfold a code section with the Toggle Fold command.
Fold or unfold recursively with the Toggle Fold Recursively Command

allSteps.title: Use Intellisense to improve coding efficiency

nodes: Intellisense suggestions can be opened with the Trigger Intellisense command.
Inline intellisense suggestions can be triggered with Trigger Inline Suggestion
Useful settings include editor.inlineCompletionsAccessibilityVerbose and editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion.
Accessibility settings can be configured by running the Open Accessibility Settings command.
